# Universal Web Foundation

Start with AGENTS.md and FOUNDATION_MANIFEST.yaml. UWF is a Foundation-first planning and governance workspace for web projects. Application code is prohibited until the relevant implementation gate is approved.

Documentation:
- README.md — human installation and overview
- Foundation/README.md — Foundation stage map
- Foundation/00-Control — questions, decisions, risks, and change records
- Foundation/14-Change-Management — reviewable scope changes, impact analysis, and release backlog
- Foundation/06-UX-UI — optional creative brief, responsive/accessibility review, and simulation plan
- Foundation/00-Control/Capability-Matrix.md — honest workflow maturity and known limits
- Foundation/06-UX-UI/Design-Reference-Registry.md, Reference-Analysis.md, and FigCraft-Reference-Catalog.md — clean-room UI/UX reference analysis
- Foundation/12-Handover/Release-Readiness.md — evidence before calling an implementation release stable
- Foundation/15-Engineering-Materials — catalog, lifecycle, and required Composition Manifest
- Foundation/16-External-Reference-Evidence — source policy, evidence cards, trust, and provenance
- Foundation/17-Research-Content-Operations — taxonomy, source-led content, scale/batch, rights, and publish controls
- agent/ — Orchestrator, routing, question budget, assumptions, status, and escalation
- tools/ — tool contracts, local dry-run runner, validators, action gates, and adapter boundaries
- policies/ — permissions, data, research, publishing, automation, and runtime limits
- evaluations/ — scenarios, expected artifacts, negative tests, and regression checks
- templates/ — reusable specifications and review formats
- docs/ — beginner, professional, automation, and migration guides

Terminal-agent workflow: read AGENTS.md and FOUNDATION_MANIFEST.yaml, then use `uwf context --json`, `uwf status --json`, `uwf next --json`, and `uwf validate --json`. Never implement application code before the developer approves the implementation gate.

Use `uwf template list` for original Foundation starter packs, `uwf reference` before using external references, `uwf capability` before promising a capability, and `uwf release check` before describing an implementation release as stable.

Before web/GitHub research or external writes, prepare and complete a truthful runtime profile. Use `uwf compose plan` for material decisions. UWF's CLI creates governance artifacts; it does not itself search the web or publish content.

The Foundation Orchestrator is the only agent-facing coordinator. It should make visible safe assumptions and ask no more than three high-impact questions at once. Use `uwf tool run ID --dry-run` before any tool-based recommendation and record the result in the Action Journal.

When `ui_ux.active_reference` is set, read its dedicated analysis document. Do not use an `ANALYSIS_REQUIRED` reference to generate a simulation or implementation.

Use `uwf reference complete figcraft` or `uwf reference complete custom` only after the analysis has a source, category, abstract lesson, original response, and developer decision.
